title: The first printing, July 4–5, 1776
note: The surviving printed broadside and the dispatch of copies on July 5. Historical print-run and survivor counts are intentionally omitted.

title: Jefferson's original Rough draught
note: Draft, alterations by Adams and Franklin, and congressional revisions. The approved text preceded the later engrossed parchment.

title: Franklin, printer and writer
note: Primary printed examples of Poor Richard's Almanack and Franklin's printing work.

title: Washington's copy of the Declaration
institution: Library of Congress, George Washington Papers
note: Hancock sent the printed Declaration to Washington on July 6; Washington had it read to the troops in New York on July 9.

title: The Federalist in historic newspapers
note: Essays by Hamilton, Madison and Jay under Publius, supporting ratification in 1787–1788; the guide indexes original newspaper printings.

title: Printing the Declaration of Independence
institution: Library of Congress, Rare Book and Special Collections
note: The approved wording was sent to Dunlap's shop; the first printing belongs to the evening of July 4 and early July 5.

title: Declaring Independence: drafting the documents
note: The vote for independence on July 2, adoption on July 4, and the later engrossed copy ordered July 19 and signed beginning August 2.

title: The Odyssey, Book I
note: The sheet presents an extract from the invocation, ending at “safely home”; the source sentence continues.

title: The Gospel according to St Matthew
note: Matthew 5:3–12 and 16:26. Modern-spelling KJV transcription; 1611 identifies the translation, not a facsimile of its original spelling.

title: Confessions, Book I
credit: Augustine / translated by E. B. Pusey
note: The opening prayer addresses God. The broadside extracts the clause beginning “Thou madest us”.

title: Inferno, Canto I, lines 1–3
credit: Dante / translated by Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, 1867
note: The first tercet. Line breaks and the capital “For” follow the text file used to typeset the existing sheet.

title: Christ Preaching (The Hundred Guilder Print)
credit: Rembrandt van Rijn / c. 1649 / National Gallery of Art
note: Object 9969. Open-access image in the public domain. The work is an etching, drypoint and burin on Japan paper.

title: Aristotle with a Bust of Homer
credit: Rembrandt van Rijn / 1653 / The Metropolitan Museum of Art
note: Object 437394. Public-domain image. Aristotle rests his hand on a bust of Homer.

title: The Circle of the Lustful: Paolo and Francesca
credit: William Blake / 1827 / National Gallery of Art
note: Object 797. Open-access image in the public domain. An engraving after Dante’s Inferno, Canto V.
